message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip or reorder sections if you already have some components or experience.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. |
| 2 | **Choose a Case** | Determines airflow, size, aesthetics, and future upgrade space. | ATX mid‑tower is a safe bet; make sure it has enough drive bays and cable management options. |
| 3 | **Pick a Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components; must be reliable and efficient. | Look for 80+ Bronze or better, 80+ Gold if you’re serious. Size should fit the case (ATX, SFX, etc.). |
| 4 | **Select a Motherboard** | Hosts CPU, RAM, storage, expansion slots, and connectivity. | Match the socket to your CPU (e.g., LGA 1700 for Intel 12th‑gen). Check BIOS support for your chosen CPU. |
| 5 | **Choose a CPU** | The brain of your PC; determines performance for tasks. | For gaming: AMD Ryzen 5/7 or Intel i5/i7. For content creation: higher core counts (Ryzen 9, i9). |
| 6 | **Get RAM** | Speed and capacity affect multitasking and future‑proofing. | DDR4 3200‑3600 MHz is common; 16 GB is minimum for gaming, 32 GB for heavy workloads. |
| 7 | **Pick Storage** | SSDs are fast; HDDs add cheap bulk. | NVMe M.2 SSD for OS + games; SATA SSD/HDD for mass storage. |
| 8 | **Select a GPU (if needed)** | Handles graphics; essential for gaming, 3D rendering, or GPU‑accelerated tasks. | For gaming: RTX 3060/3070 or AMD RX 6700/6800. For office: integrated graphics may suffice. |
| 9 | **Choose an Operating System** | Windows, Linux, or macOS (via Hackintosh). | Windows 11 Home/Pro is most common; Linux is free and great for developers. |
|10 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Screwdrivers, anti‑static wristband, cable ties, clean surface. | Work on a non‑metal table or a static‑free mat. |
|11 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, install standoffs, set up cable management. | Keep the case open and organized; label cables for easier troubleshooting. |
|12 | **Install the PSU** | Mount it, connect the main 24‑pin and CPU 8‑pin connectors. | Make sure cables are routed neatly to avoid airflow obstruction. |
|13 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align with standoffs, secure screws, attach I/O shield. | Double‑check that all screws are tight but not over‑tightened. |
|14 | **Install the CPU** | Lift the socket lever, align the CPU, lower gently, lock lever. | Use thermal paste (or pre‑applied) before mounting the cooler. |
|15 | **Attach the CPU Cooler** | Mount fan or liquid cooler, connect fan header or pump. | Ensure proper airflow direction (intake at front, exhaust at rear). |
|16 | **Insert RAM** | Snap into DIMM slots, click until locked. | Install in matched pairs for dual‑channel mode. |
|17 | **Mount Storage** | Secure SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | Connect SATA data & power cables if using SATA drives. |
|18 | **Install the GPU** | Insert into PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect power cables. | Ensure the slot is fully seated; use a small screwdriver to tighten. |
|19 | **Connect Front Panel & USB** | Attach power button, reset, USB headers, audio jack. | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pin layout. |
|20 | **Cable Management** | Tidy up cables, use ties or Velcro straps. | Keep cables away from fans and airflow paths. |
|21 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Power on, enter BIOS (usually F2, DEL, or ESC). | Set boot order, enable XMP for RAM, check temperatures. |
|22 | **Install Operating System** | Create bootable USB, install OS, update drivers. | Install chipset, GPU, and other drivers first. |
|23 | **Test & Benchmark** | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark), benchmark (Cinebench, 3DMark). | Monitor temperatures; ensure stability. |
|24 | **Final Tweaks** | Adjust fan curves, set RGB lighting, install additional software. | Keep system clean; schedule regular updates. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Case
- [ ] PSU
- [ ] Motherboard
- [ ] CPU
- [ ] RAM
- [ ] Storage (NVMe + SATA)
- [ ] GPU (if needed)
- [ ] OS
- [ ] Tools (screwdriver, anti‑static wristband)
- [ ] Cable ties / Velcro straps
- [ ] Thermal paste (if not pre‑applied)

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wristband; never touch metal parts while components are powered. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow; use quality thermal paste; keep dust out. |
| **Component incompatibility** | Verify socket, chipset, and BIOS support before buying. |
| **Loose screws** | Tighten all screws, but avoid overtightening which can strip threads. |
| **Cable clutter** | Plan cable routing early; use cable ties or Velcro straps. |

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build & price comparison tool.
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.
- **Forums** – Tom’s Hardware, Reddit r/buildapc, r/pcmasterrace.

Happy building! If you hit a snag or need component recommendations, just let me know.
